body.text: Joachim moves to Bahrain from Mangaluru. His nephew, Darrel, wants to do the same, without realising the trials and tribulations of immigrant life.
The book traces the life of a young Indian clerk in Heidelberg in 1916. After meeting a mysterious revolutionary, he finds himself entangled in a plot for freedom operated by Indians in exile.
The Haunting of Dr. Shamsi and Other Unsettling Tales
The horror stories set in Pakistan straddle the old world and the new, the realm of science and that of the unexplained. The stories are drawn from true accounts.
Courting equality: Landmark Cases in the Battle for Women’s Rights

Discover the landmark women’s rights cases of the past 50 years that redefined justice in India. From anti-dowry agitations to the Shah Bano and Nirbhaya cases, these cases compel us to confront what equality means and how far we still have to go.

This scholarly exploration of monster-making through the ages—from Minotaurs to Muppets, dwarfs to dragons—exposes how humanity has always turned any “difference” into monstrosity, and uncovers the chilling history of what we fear the most.
Peasants: Makers of the Modern World

Four crops, three continents, two billion peasants: this is the hidden world we all depend upon for survival. Focussing on rice, sugarcane, coca, and cocoa, Maryam Aslany offers a comprehensive portrait of rural crisis in the neoliberal era.
